issues.reason: The half that stands is the coined scale: 'decline' replaces the stated 'down' with an unstated synonym, which the Measure rule ('record what's said') and the standing no-synonym discipline both bar; the half that overstates is the phrasal-verb citation — 'finished down' is compositional and paradigmatic (finished down / up / flat / higher), not a non-compositional particle verb like go_out, so finish_down is not mandated and the bare 'finish' class stands.

Here the clause states no dimension word at all, so nothing was swapped out — this is the uncovered closing-level construction the reviewer records as a gap, and (Measure sk_finish_1 value 9317.64 point) is true and well-typed, with 'points' supplied by the same sentence; the calibration line protects the improvisation.

gaps_confirmed: an index's closing level and session change ('finished down 31.23 points ... at 9,317.64') — Measure needs a surface dimension word for its scale, and 'at' supplies none
appositive / equivalence 'or' restating one quantity in another unit ('31.23 points, or 0.33 percent') — Disjunction covers genuine alternatives only, and an (Or ...) would be wrong here
a ticker / identifier code in apposition to a name ('.DJI') — no head records it and the exactly-one-Name rule blocks a second Name atom, so it is dropped
new_gaps: 'finished down / up / flat' — a predicative secondary complement of a verb of ending, with a measure phrase hanging off it ('down 31.23 points'): it is neither a resultative state result nor a manner adverb, and no slot holds the change amount as distinct from the level
repair_summary: Replaced the coined scale 'decline' with the stated surface word 'down' in both change measures (points and percent); left the event class, the closing-level measure and every other atom untouched.
notes: Patient on the intransitive subject of 'finish' is left as the parser had it — the reviewer flagged it only as a judgment call, and the change-of-state reading is defensible. Both change atoms are the same fact in two units, which is faithful to the appositive 'or' and asserts nothing extra.
